source_name: Fond penzijskog i invalidskog osiguranja Crne Gore (Fond PIO) — javne nabavke section
why_relevant: Pension fund: the counterparty behind mass recurring disbursements (pension payouts) that flow through banks and the post office counter network. Its site carries public procurement, analytical cards (analitičke kartice) and regulations sections — a buyer feed plus a disbursement-channel signal.

source_name: Vodovod i kanalizacija d.o.o. Podgorica — plan javnih nabavki / hitne nabavke
why_relevant: Capital-city water utility and a sector contracting authority (water management). Publishes procurement plan, emergency procurements, the named procurement officer, and — payments-relevant — runs consumer billing and account-balance checking services (provjera stanja računa, prijava stanja), i.e. a collection/self-service estate. Template for the ~20 municipal ViK utilities country-wide.

source_name: Komunalne usluge d.o.o. Podgorica (municipal utility services)
why_relevant: City-owned utility (public lighting, traffic signalling and related communal services) founded by the Podgorica city assembly. Represents the municipal-SOE buyer layer that procures locally and publishes on its own site. Lower payments intensity than EPCG/Pošta, but part of the complete buyer map for the cell.

source_name: Čistoća d.o.o. Podgorica (waste utility)
why_relevant: Podgorica waste-collection utility and a buyer in the municipal SOE layer. No independent website surfaced in this pass; its public communication runs largely through Facebook, and it is represented on the Chamber of Commerce utility association board. Track mainly via CeJN and the chamber association rather than a self-published tender page.

source_name: Tender Monitor (tender-monitor.com) — commercial monitoring of the state procurement portal
why_relevant: A commercial service that monitors the state public procurement portal on subscribers' behalf. Relevant as a ready-made alternative to building a CeJN scraper against a JS-rendered SPA, and as evidence of what filtering dimensions the local market considers useful (buyer, CPV, keyword).

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore — Udruženje komunalne privrede (Chamber of Commerce, utilities association)
why_relevant: The association board membership is effectively a directory of Montenegro's municipal utility SOEs and their senior officers (e.g. Čistoća d.o.o. Podgorica is represented on the board). This is the cheapest route to a complete municipal-utility actor list for buyers that have weak or no web presence, and it snowballs into named contacts.

source_name: CBCG — Tenderi i oglasi (Tenders and Notices), Montenegrin site
source_subtype: central bank own procurement/tender notice page
why_relevant: The Central Bank of Montenegro's own tender/public-call page and the single most cell-specific source. Observed live listings include the 2026 public call for marketing and UX strategy services for the instant payments (TIPS Clone) rollout, 2025 calls for TIPS Clone connectivity services and pre-implementation technical support, jubilee coin design competitions, and construction/technical-documentation calls. Because CBCG publishes here rather than only on the national CEJN portal, anyone scanning only the national portal misses these payments-infrastructure notices.

source_name: CBCG — Instant plaćanja (TIPS Clone) programme page
why_relevant: Programme page for Montenegro's instant payments platform (live since July 2026, built on the Banca d'Italia TIPS Clone with ECB and World Bank support, all 11 domestic banks onboarded). Announces phases, participants and go-live milestones that precede and follow procurement — an early-warning indicator for upcoming CBCG payments-infrastructure tenders.

source_name: CBCG — RTGS system / CBCG payment system pages (RTS/X)
why_relevant: Documents the national RTGS and the RTS/X new-generation payment system (ISO 20022 aligned, launched 2025) — the largest functional/technological change to the national payment system since 2005. Establishes what infrastructure exists, what vendor generation it belongs to, and therefore what CBCG will next need to procure or upgrade.

source_name: CBCG — Pristup informacijama (Free Access to Information)
why_relevant: CBCG's FOI (Zakon o slobodnom pristupu informacijama) entry point, including a public-registers/records subsection. This is the legal channel to request procurement plans, contracts and award decisions that CBCG does not proactively publish — important because no dedicated 'plan javnih nabavki' page was found on cbcg.me.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal — EC-ENEST (Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood) calls covering Montenegro
why_relevant: Highest-value finding for this cell: the CBCG treasury/cash-handling equipment procurement (supply, delivery, positioning and installation of new banknote/coin processing, euro-authentication and gold-testing equipment for CBCG) is being run as an EU-funded open procedure under EC-ENEST references, not on the national portal. Reference EC-ENEST/TGD/2026/EA-LOP/0101 with a 7 October 2026 deadline supersedes an almost identically named EC-ENEST/TGD/2026/EA-LOP/0005 published 3 February 2026. Montenegro's Ministry of Finance is the administering side. Anyone monitoring only cbcg.me or CEJN misses this entirely.

source_name: World Bank — Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA alignment (TIPS Clone) project, P509405
source_subtype: IFI project page with procurement plan and contract awards
why_relevant: The EUR 8 million World Bank loan financing Montenegro's TIPS Clone / SEPA alignment work. World Bank operations publish a Procurement Plan and, in STEP, contract awards — so this is the authoritative pipeline of what CBCG will buy for instant payments, at what value, and who won. It also explains why some CBCG notices use World Bank selection methods (the observed CQS-25 Request for Expression of Interest is Consultant Qualification Selection).

source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports — Montenegro financial infrastructure and FSAP technical notes
why_relevant: Project appraisal documents, FSAP technical notes on Montenegro's financial infrastructure, and implementation reports describe the state of RTGS/settlement systems and the planned modernisation components. These name components before they become tenders, and are the best diagnostic material for judging what CBCG's payment infrastructure actually lacks.

source_name: eKapija Montenegro — Centralna banka Crne Gore company/tender feed
source_subtype: business news / tender portal with entity feed
why_relevant: Business news and tender portal with a dedicated CBCG topic stream and company profile. Reports CBCG tenders and contract news in business terms (values, winners, reconstruction and IT contracts) and often earlier or with more commercial detail than the official notice.

source_name: Borba.me and Dan.co.me — investigative reporting on CBCG procurement specifications
why_relevant: Montenegrin outlets that scrutinise CBCG's procurement plan line items and tender technical specifications (e.g. reporting that a vehicle tender's specifications appeared to be written around a single model). Valuable both as evidence that a CBCG plan javnih nabavki exists and circulates, and as a signal of specification-steering — relevant when assessing whether a CBCG payments or cash-handling tender is genuinely contestable.

source_name: CBCG — Strateški plan 2025–2028 (Strategic Plan)
why_relevant: CBCG's own multi-year strategy naming the payment-system, SEPA-alignment, cash-operations and IT modernisation objectives that generate procurement. Best available forward-looking proxy for a procurement pipeline given that no public procurement plan page was found.

source_name: EBRD ECEPP — Electronic Contracts and Procurement Portal, Montenegro notices
why_relevant: EBRD-financed procurement in Montenegro is published here rather than on CEJN. Relevant as an alternative IFI channel for financial-infrastructure and IT procurement involving Montenegrin public bodies; an EBRD Montenegro notice surfaced during the EC-ENEST search, confirming the portal indexes ME notices.

source_name: DevelopmentAid — CBCG organisation profile (tender/award history for donor-funded work)
why_relevant: Aggregates donor- and IFI-funded tenders, awards and partner relationships for CBCG as an entity. Useful for reconstructing which international consultancies and vendors have already worked on CBCG payments and cash projects — a shortcut to the incumbent map.

source_name: CBCG — Saopštenja (press releases) and social channels
source_subtype: institutional press release feed + social media
why_relevant: CBCG announces go-lives, project phases, vendor cooperation and infrastructure milestones in press releases and on LinkedIn/X/Facebook before or instead of formal procurement documents. Fastest low-cost trigger for 'a procurement probably happened or is about to'.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (Supplement to the Official Journal of the EU)
source_subtype: official tender gazette / procurement notice database
why_relevant: Mandatory publication venue for EU external-action (IPA) contract notices, prior information notices and contract award notices concerning Montenegro, and for EIB-financed project procurement outside the EU. Covers financial-sector IT, payment systems and public financial management assignments tendered by the EU Delegation to Montenegro and by Montenegrin contracting authorities under EU rules. Structured, searchable, with CPV codes and open bulk/API access.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal (SEDIA) — external actions calls and tenders
why_relevant: Single entry point for EC-managed procurement and grants, including PRAG-governed external-action service/supply contracts for IPA beneficiaries such as Montenegro. Carries call documentation (ToRs) that TED abstracts omit — ToRs are the richest description of what payments/PFM systems the EU intends to fund.

source_name: Delegation of the European Union to Montenegro — tenders and calls
source_subtype: donor country office / contracting authority page
why_relevant: The EU Delegation directly launches, awards and manages a large share of IPA contracts in Montenegro under PRAG, and publishes/mirrors its own calls for tenders. It is the contracting authority for many digital-government and PFM technical-assistance contracts, and it publishes bilingual (en/me) news items naming projects and beneficiaries before formal notices appear.

source_name: European Commission DG NEAR — Montenegro financial assistance under IPA
why_relevant: Authoritative programming layer: annual/multiannual IPA action documents for Montenegro state which sectors (public financial management, digital public services, payments) will be tendered 12-24 months ahead. Best early-warning source for pipeline before any notice exists.
